links.note: Machine-readable record written after the data, transcribing PROTOCOL.md (holdout section, addendum A, addendum B frozen in 6a14c3d before native computation) and amendments 1-2 (after the data). Not a preregistration in this form.
links.amendment_history: PROTOCOL.md amendments 1-2, both filed after the data they affect: (1) B1 tail recalibrated by Monte Carlo, 0.8283 -> 0.8313; (2) controls PC1 and PC2 added. The cells they affect (B1 p-value, PC1, PC2) decide nothing under the experiment-protocol rules.
links.freeze_evidence: The only pre-data freeze is git commit 6a14c3d8bd (PROTOCOL.md addendum B, pushed before any native computation). The holdout section and addendum A were frozen only in a scratchpad file (sha256 3181538d..., 19b23a6e...) before their computation; no commit records that. This JSON record was written after all data and is left as a draft, not frozen, because freezing would assert a pre-data analysis plan that did not exist.

question: Do the post-hoc NIST seed skip-rule separators hold out of sample, and does any mechanism (Schoof/SEA branch structure, Elkies coverage) make an independent prediction that the data supports?

claims.text: Within-stream permutation tail probabilities of L_E, sign(t), and the l<200 Elkies decompositions on the 21 prime candidates are as recorded in out/summary.txt (exact enumeration of 4,480 assignments).
B2: no set S of odd primes l <= 100 has all 10 published curves Atkin at every l in S while covering the 11 skipped curves.
B1: the NSA binary curves' mean L_E percentile is not above 50 under the Gekeler model.
Any statement about the historical skip rule.

hypotheses.statement: Skipped candidates have a larger Elkies bound L_E (expensive SEA abandoned).
hypotheses.mechanism: An Elkies-only SEA needs Elkies primes up to L_E; costly counts were abandoned.

data_seen.measured: H1 Elkies coverage lean on the same 21 curves (p = 0.008), learned after Addendum A

hypotheses.statement: An isogeny-structure filter also ran in the NSA binary pipeline.
hypotheses.mechanism: The published prime curves sit high in L_E; the same filter would raise the binary curves.

predictions.minimum_effect: mean percentile > 50 with small tail probability

hypotheses.statement: The historical SEA failed when some prime in a fixed set S was Elkies.
hypotheses.mechanism: A buggy Elkies step skips curves with more Elkies primes, matching the observed direction.

data_seen.measured: H1 Elkies coverage lean on the same 21 curves (p = 0.008), learned after Addendum A

arms.description: the 21 valid 1997-98 prime candidates (10 published, 11 skipped), inputs/historical.tsv
NSA binary curves B-233/283/409/571 (primary) and B-163 (secondary), inputs/binary.tsv
PC1: smallest-L_E labels planted in every stream (amendment 2)
Gekeler-model draws: the 4,480-assignment null for permutation tests and the 20,000-replicate calibration for B1; PC2 power
control_null.gp: the Gekeler model against exact ellcard counts at 64 and 80 bits; not run (checkpoint gate, no S3 credential)

aa.not_applicable_reason: deterministic exact computation on fixed inputs with a fixed seed: reruns are byte-identical (verified), so there is no run-to-run noise floor

positive.expected_detection: P(<=obs) equal to the smallest attainable value

null_population.description: count-preserving label assignments of the 21 prime candidates; Gekeler-model L_E draws per field
null_population.generator: exact enumeration (assignments) and nullLE() in mechanism.gp with setrand(20261026)
null_population.why_n: every assignment that keeps each seed run's published count is enumerated; Monte Carlo draws are 20,000 per field

factors.name: rng_seed
factors.how: setrand at the top of mechanism.gp

factors.name: prime_bound
factors.value: LMAX 3000 for L_E, l<200 decomposition, l<=100 for B2

factors.name: analyst
factors.how: unblinded single analyst who had seen the labels and the 2026-10-25 report; recorded in the README

randomization.arm_order_reason: exact computation with no timing; order cannot affect any value

seed_derivation.note: single fixed GP seed written in addendum B before computation

instance_sampling.rule: all curves in the two frozen input tables

blinding.how: not masked: published/skipped labels are public and were seen

power.note: the permutation tests enumerate all 4,480 assignments (smallest attainable one-sided P 0.00022, from PC1); B1 has marginal power at the published-prime effect size (PC2: P = 0.045 at mean 74.6)

primary.name: tail probability
primary.definition: exact permutation tail over 4,480 count-preserving assignments, or the add-one Monte Carlo tail for B1/PC2

primary.name: skipped curves not covered by S_max

secondary.name: test statistic
secondary.definition: skipped rank-sum within streams, or mean Gekeler-null percentile
secondary.formula: rank-sum: sum over skipped rows of the within-stream average rank of the feature; mean percentile: (1/k) sum_i pct(V_field(i), L_E(i))

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: one pass of mechanism.gp over the frozen inputs

invalidation_rules: a B1 or figure percentile is model-dependent until control_null.gp passes
control_null.gp runs only after a resume checkpoint uploads (repository gate); until then the null model is unvalidated

decision_rule.text: H2 and B1 are supported only if their one-sided tail is below 0.025 (Bonferroni over 2). B2 is supported only if 0 skipped curves are uncovered. Effects found in the reverse direction are reported as post hoc and decide nothing.

graphs: mechanism.svg: L_E percentiles per stream and for the binary curves

inadmissible: reading the reverse-direction L_E effect as confirmatory
counting the SEC 2 curves as a test of the NSA generator
quoting B1 percentiles as model-free before control_null.gp passes

literature.claim: H1 Elkies coverage already preregistered L_E; lean p = 0.008

literature.ref: E.-U. Gekeler, Frobenius distributions of elliptic curves over finite prime fields, IMRN 2003
literature.claim: Frobenius mod l is distributed like a random GL2(F_l) matrix with det q
